reports.title: Alexander Tostevin: Prevention of future deaths report

promises.quote: case. I will address each area in turn. Disclosure of information between DCMH and the Chain of Command. DCMH operates as an independent organisation, which sits within Defence Primary Healthcare (DPHC), a Tri-Service organisation in UK Strategic Command. Although military DCMH staff2 are drawn from the medical services of the Royal Navy (RN), Army and Royal Air Force (RAF), DCMH is independent of all three Service chains of command. promises.summary: DCMH is independent of all three Service chains of command

concerns.quote: The medical care provided to service personnel through the DCMH is not truly independent, in that personal medical information may be disclosed to Chain of Command where substantial public interest demands disclosure, particularly for the protection of the operational capability of the Unit and the safety of other Unit personnel. This is, of course, unlike mental health care provided in a civilian context. The evidence heard at the Inquest was that this lack of independence risks service personnel

There is no single composite risk assessment and care plan for service users that draws tooether all the relevant information for 2 a service user and identifies the plan in place (care plan and risk management plan) at any given time. Such as document is often used in other care settings, including mental health trusts.
concerns.hazard: absence of composite risk assessment and care plan

concerns.quote: The lack of independence of DCMH risks service users minimising and/or under reporting the risks they may pose to themselves for fear that information may be disclosed to the Chain of Command. If the true extent of the risk of is not known by DCMH, an effective risk management plan to mitigate the risk of cannot be formulated.

concerns.quote: army VRM guidance does not invite those attending case conferences to consider 'checking in' or meeting those assessed as posing a risk of self-harm on return to their unit
concerns.hazard: risk of self-harm on return to unit

concerns.quote: suicide prevention training is not mandatory for army welfare officers/welfare NCOs
concerns.hazard: insufficient suicide prevention training for welfare officers

concerns.quote: insufficient focus in that training on the actual aim including reducing risk and preventing suicide
concerns.hazard: insufficient focus on reducing risk and preventing suicide in VRM training

concerns.quote: information sharing between medical and command personnel poses challenges
lack of detail contained within the case conference notes hindered this inquest's ability to establish precisely what risk information was shared
concerns.hazard: lack of detail in case conference notes

concerns.quote: information contained about relevant protective factors and safety actions is not necessarily shared with the Chain of Command
concerns.hazard: information not shared with Chain of Command

links.explanation: Both reports highlight problems with how mental‑health information is handled between defence medical services and the Chain of Command. The earlier report warns that lack of independence leads to non‑disclosure fears, while the later report notes that protective‑factor information is not routinely shared with the Chain of Command.
links.earlier_quote: The medical care provided to service personnel through the DCMH is not truly independent, in that personal medical information may be disclosed to Chain of Command where substantial public interest demands disclosure
links.later_quote: I was concerned to hear that when a risk management and safety plan has been prepared by the Defence mental health services the information contained about relevant protective factors and safety actions is not necessarily shared with the Chain of Command.
